participation.context: Read the Rose's bill and the Theatre's, and did not take either down.
participation.name: William Shakespeare

story.body: You read what the post was willing to say. Two kings. No author. No takings. You went on toward the gate.

title: Read the Rose's Longshanks and Thursday's Richard the Second

participation.context: Let the title do the work, and did not add the plot.
participation.name: William Shakespeare

participation.context: Heard the bill succeed with a stranger, and moved them on.
participation.name: Abel Garnish

participation.context: Counted two kings and none of them his, and was content.
participation.name: Will Kemp

story.body: You heard the carter say Thursday. You did not tell him the story, and you did not tell him the author. Garnish called the post finished. Kemp kept walking.

title: Heard a carter call it a king play

participation.context: Kept the second reading, refused a third, and left Kemp off the plot.
participation.name: William Shakespeare

participation.context: Walked the lists, and confirmed Kemp is not on the plot.
participation.name: Abel Garnish

participation.context: Said the prison speech twice to an empty house.
participation.name: Richard Burbage

participation.context: Asked after the gown, and was told it does not show.
participation.name: Nick Sorrell

participation.context: Asked after the sweet tooth, and kept to you, not thou.
participation.name: Will Kemp

relations.note: the hem is not the play

story.body: You let Burbage say the line twice and did not add a third. You told Nick the gown does not show. You answered Kemp's tooth with Thursday, and with no part for him in the king.

relations.note: the hem is not the play

title: Heard Burbage say the prison speech twice
